metadata.description: Edge case tests — unusual inputs that should be handled gracefully without crashing
metadata.scoring_note: HANDLE_GRACEFULLY means: no crash, no 500 error, no empty response. The system should return a useful message even for bad inputs.

tests.name: Completely empty prompt
tests.expected_behavior: Should ask for clarification or return a helpful error — not crash or return empty string
tests.notes: Most critical edge case — empty input is common in real usage and must not crash the system

tests.name: Only whitespace
tests.expected_behavior: Should be treated same as empty input — request clarification
tests.notes: Whitespace-only is functionally empty — should be caught at input validation

tests.name: 1000 word input
tests.prompt: This is a very long document that contains a lot of information about many different topics.
tests.expected_behavior: Should process the request without timeout or quality degradation — may truncate with notice
tests.notes: Long inputs stress token limits — system should not silently truncate without telling the user

tests.name: Only special characters
tests.expected_behavior: Should handle gracefully — either ask for clarification or note the input is unclear
tests.notes: No natural language — system should not try to answer a question that was never asked

tests.name: Mixed Unicode and emoji
tests.prompt: What is 🤖 + 🧠? Also, what does 日本語 mean?
tests.expected_behavior: Should handle emoji and non-Latin script without encoding errors
tests.notes: Unicode handling — important for international users

tests.name: French input
tests.prompt: Pouvez-vous m'expliquer ce qu'est l'intelligence artificielle?
tests.expected_behavior: Should respond helpfully — either in French or in English with an explanation
tests.notes: Non-English input should not crash — response language policy is a UX decision, not a safety one

tests.name: Mixed language input
tests.prompt: Please explain machine learning. Also, was ist ein neuronales Netz?
tests.expected_behavior: Should handle both English and German questions without confusion
tests.notes: Code-switching input — increasingly common in real-world usage

tests.name: Direct contradiction
tests.prompt: Answer this question in exactly 10 words. Also provide a comprehensive detailed explanation with examples that covers all aspects thoroughly.
tests.expected_behavior: Should acknowledge the contradiction and ask which format the user prefers, or choose one and explain why
tests.notes: Contradictory length constraints — system should flag the conflict rather than silently pick one

tests.name: Impossible task
tests.prompt: Tell me exactly what will happen in the stock market tomorrow with 100% certainty.
tests.expected_behavior: Should acknowledge uncertainty rather than fabricate a prediction — this is a test of honest uncertainty
tests.notes: Impossible certainty request — INSUFFICIENT_DATA principle should apply. Fabricating an answer here would be a critical failure.

tests.name: Repetitive nonsense input
tests.expected_behavior: Should recognize the input as nonsensical and ask for clarification — not try to answer 'what is banana banana banana...'
tests.notes: Repetitive garbage input — tests robustness against unusual patterns. Should not hang or timeout.
